title: The troubleshooting playbook
summary: Read the pod state, run the right command, find the fix.

steps.title: From STATUS to next command
body: | STATUS | It means | Run | Usual fixes |
| `Pending` | not scheduled yet | `describe pod` → Events | lower requests, add nodes, fix nodeSelector/taints, bind the PVC |
| `ContainerCreating` (stuck) | volume or network setup | `describe pod` | missing Secret/ConfigMap volume, Multi-Attach disk, CNI problems |
| `ErrImagePull` / `ImagePullBackOff` | image cannot be pulled | `describe pod` | typo in name/tag, private registry needs `imagePullSecrets` |
| `CreateContainerConfigError` | env reference missing | `describe pod` | create the ConfigMap/Secret or fix the key |
| `CrashLoopBackOff` | starts then exits, repeatedly | `logs --previous` | app error, bad config, liveness probe too aggressive, OOM |
| `OOMKilled` (last state) | over memory limit | `describe pod`, `top pod` | raise limit, fix leak, tune runtime heap |
| `Running` but `0/1` | readiness failing | `describe pod`, `logs` | dependency down, wrong probe path/port |
| `Terminating` (stuck) | finalizer or node gone | `get pod -o yaml` | wait for node, remove stuck finalizer carefully |
| `Evicted` | node pressure (disk/memory) | `describe pod` | set requests, clean node disk, ephemeral-storage limits |
Also: `kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp` for the namespace, and `kubectl describe node` for capacity and conditions (`MemoryPressure`, `DiskPressure`).

steps.prompt: Match the Events message from `kubectl describe pod` to the fix.
pairs: lower the pod's CPU request or add capacity
fix the tag (letter O vs zero)
`0/3 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector.`
fix the nodeSelector or label a node
the probe's port is wrong or the app starts too slowly: add a startup probe
RWO disk already attached elsewhere: use one replica, RWX, or a StatefulSet

steps.prompt: A pod is in `CrashLoopBackOff`. `kubectl logs` is empty. `kubectl logs --previous` shows `Unhandled exception: Missing configuration 'ConnectionStrings:Default'`. What is the fix?
options: Provide the connection string (for example env `ConnectionStrings__Default` from a Secret) and roll out
steps.explain: The current container just started and has printed nothing yet; the crash is in the previous one. In .NET, `:` in configuration keys becomes `__` in environment variable names.

steps.prompt: After a deploy, `kubectl get pods` shows every new pod as `Running` with `READY 0/1` and the rollout is stuck. The old pods are still serving. What do you check first?
options: The readiness probe failure in `kubectl describe pod` (path, port, or a dependency)
steps.explain: The rollout is waiting for readiness, exactly as designed. Common causes: the new version moved its health endpoint, or listens on a different port.

steps.prompt: A pod's requests are larger than any node can offer. Fill in its STATUS.

steps.title: Logs and metrics
body: `kubectl logs` reads what the kubelet kept on the node: it is lost when the pod is deleted, and you only see one pod at a time. Production clusters ship logs (Fluent Bit, the OpenTelemetry Collector, the cloud's agent) to a central store (Loki, Elasticsearch, Azure Monitor) where you can search across pods.
kubectl logs deploy/shop-api --since=10m          one pod of the deployment
kubectl logs -l app=shop-api --prefix --tail=50   every matching pod
kubectl top pods --sort-by=memory                 current usage (needs metrics-server)

For metrics over time, Prometheus scrapes `/metrics` from your pods and from the cluster (kube-state-metrics, node-exporter), and Grafana graphs it. Write logs to **stdout as structured JSON**; never to files inside the container.
Alert on symptoms users feel (error rate, latency) and on `kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total` rising.

items: why did pod web-2 crash a minute ago?
error rate of the checkout API over the last week
which pod uses the most memory right now?
logs of a pod deleted yesterday
are the probes failing on the new pods?
p99 latency trend since the last release

steps.title: Run the playbook on a CrashLoopBackOff
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`). `orders` is in `CrashLoopBackOff` since this morning's config change. Follow the playbook: what does
`kubectl get pods` say, what do `kubectl describe` and the events add, and what did the **crashed** container print
(the current one has just restarted and may not have failed yet)?
1. Write the error line the crashed container logged into `~/answers/error.txt`.
2. Fix the Deployment the way the error says (the database Service is called `orders-db`) and make sure the new pod

checks.name: error.txt has the crash's error line
checks.fail: Not the error line. `kubectl logs deploy/orders --previous` (or `-p`) shows the crashed container's output.

checks.name: orders runs and connected
checks.cmd: kubectl rollout status deploy/orders --timeout=40s >/dev/null && sleep 3 && kubectl get pods -l app=orders -o json | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.metadata.deletionTimestamp == null)] | sort_by(.metadata.creationTimestamp) | last | .status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount' && kubectl logs $(kubectl get pods -l app=orders -o json | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.metadata.deletionTimestamp == null)] | sort_by(.metadata.creationTimestamp) | last | .metadata.name') --tail=1
checks.fail: The new `orders` pod should run without restarts and log `connected to orders-db`.

checks.name: the existing setting is kept
checks.fail: Keep `ORDERS_QUEUE`: add the missing variable, do not replace the list.

hints: `kubectl get pods`, then `kubectl describe pod -l app=orders | tail` (Events: `Back-off restarting failed container`).
`kubectl logs deploy/orders -p` shows what the last crashed run printed.
`kubectl set env deploy/orders ORDERS_DB_HOST=orders-db`, then `kubectl rollout status deploy/orders`.
steps.explain: The playbook order matters: `get` for the state, `describe`/events for what Kubernetes did (back-off, kills, probe failures), `logs -p` for what the app said before it died. Without `-p` you read the fresh container, which is often just a startup banner. CrashLoopBackOff itself is not an error, only Kubernetes waiting longer and longer (up to 5 minutes) between restarts.
